ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible architecture-to-source-to-executable assurance TODAY (given the declared toolchain: SBCL/Common Lisp, POSIX OS, standard crypto; no verified Lisp compiler exists, and B0's F*/Coq/Perennial/CompCert toolchain is blocked) is a refinement chain in which every link is either (a) a machine-checked proof replayable offline by a small proof-checker kernel, or (b) recompute-and-compare conformance between independently produced artifacts (translation validation / diverse re-verification), terminating in an explicitly enumerated, minimized, hash-committed Trusted Computing Base (proof checker, SBCL compiler+image, OS loader, hardware). No feasible system can transport a property to the executable with a smaller trust residue than this TCB, and no property is transported beyond what the weakest link carries.
derivation: Verification theory: every proof chain bottoms out in an unverified checker plus hardware — the TCB is irreducible, only minimizable (a checker that verified itself would be circular; Gödel's second incompleteness theorem blocks a system certifying its own consistency). Thompson's trusting-trust result shows compiler trust cannot be discharged by inspection of source alone; the only feasible mitigations are a verified compiler (absent for Lisp), diverse double-compilation, or independent re-execution/recompute of the artifact-level claims — hence link-type (b) is not a shortcut but the theoretical optimum for the compiler link today. Information-theoretic: a property claim about E carries at most the information transported through the chain; any claim exceeding the conjunction of link guarantees is unverifiable assertion, which H8 forbids. Therefore ceiling = machine-checked links where a checker exists + recompute-and-compare links elsewhere + committed enumerated TCB; this is RESOURCE_BOUNDED because a verified compiler (e.g., CompCert-class for Lisp) would strictly shrink the TCB, and B0's declared resources exclude it.
attainment_mechanism: Buildable now: (1) formalize the 9 admission-kernel theorems of authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp in Lean 4 — Lean runs fully offline from a vendored toolchain, sidestepping the network-403 that blocks F*/EverParse (authority-v2/toolchain/everparse.Dockerfile, perennial.Dockerfile); the proof objects and the ~small Lean kernel become release artifacts checkable by third parties (H8). (2) Commit the toolchain: authority-v2/toolchain/trusted-toolchain-manifest.sexp already exists — extend it to hash the exact SBCL binary, Lean kernel, and OS loader, binding the enumerated TCB into the census artifact-census.lisp chain. (3) Spec-to-source: generate the runtime dispatch/architecture table FROM the spec and keep the existing map≡implementation enforcement (systems/orchestrator-cli/architecture-gate.lisp ontological closure; verify-truth-gate.lisp docs≡CI) as the recompute-and-compare link. (4) Source-to-image: load-time conformance audits inside the SBCL image — the FSM coverage gate pattern in systems/orchestrator-engine-sbcl/adapters/raw-text-adapter.lisp (load-time total-coverage check) generalized to every trusted component checking its spec hash at load. (5) Image-to-verdict: kernel-diversity independent re-verification via systems/orchestrator-epistemic/release-spine.lisp + the staged L6 verifier (deploy-epistemic.lisp), which re-computes release claims in a separate execution — the diverse-execution mitigation for the unverified compiler link. (6) CDDL schemas authority-v2/schema/state.cddl and transition-certificate.cddl get a hand-written strict parser in Lisp whose test vectors are committed and cross-checked against an independent decoder (recompute-and-compare in lieu of the blocked EverParse-extracted parser).
b0_gap: This is B0's central proof-debt (map row AX-21 + §3): authority-v2 stands at 0/17 theorems PROVED and 0/13 Level-7; the kernel K, verified CDDL parser, verified checker, crash-safe store, and all 5 refinement-chain links are spec-only (F*/EverParse/Coq/Perennial/CompCert absent, network 403). Real machine-derived assurance today is confined to narrow coverage gates (FSM load-time audit, architecture-gate, verify-truth-gate). The TCB is not yet enumerated-and-hash-committed as a single artifact (trusted-toolchain-manifest.sexp exists but does not pin the running SBCL image or a proof-checker kernel), and no proof objects ship in any release, so the offline-replayable link-type (a) is entirely unrealized — the gap is precisely 'switch the formal layer from blocked-F*-plans to offline Lean 4 and bind the TCB into the release chain'.
lean_obligation: Define artifacts A (architecture spec), S (source model), E (executable image), a finite committed set TCB, transported properties P : Prop-family over traces, refinement as trace inclusion. Prove per-link and compose: theorem transport : Refines S A ∧ Conforms E S -> forall p ∈ Transported A, Assuming TCB, Holds E p, where Refines S A : forall t, Traces S t -> Traces A t is machine-checked, and Conforms E S is the recompute predicate 'the load-time audit and release-spine re-verification of E against S returned equal digests' — stated as an axiom-tagged hypothesis explicitly carried in the theorem's TCB assumptions, so the Lean statement makes the trust residue syntactically visible: no conclusion about E exists outside the Assuming TCB context.
